newsitem.title: UK: BT shares fall after MCI profit warning.
newsitem.headline: BT shares fall after MCI profit warning.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc fell by around seven percent in early trading on Friday after a profits warning from merger partner U.S. carrier MCI Communications Corp.
BT shares were trading down 31-1/2 pence at 446 after an early low of 439.

The company said late on Thursday that it is in talks with MCI on the change in outlook on the group's results after MCI said its earnings would be hit by delays in gaining entry to U.S. local phone markets.
Analysts were expecting to downgrade BT profit forecasts following the news.
Mike Stiles at Credit Lyonnais Laing said his forecast for the year to March 1999 would go down to nearer four billion pounds from the current forecast of 4.35 billion.
"We are looking for ten percent below what we thought before and so it is logical to knock the shares down ten percent," Stiles said.
Analysts said the key thing was to watch was what MCI shares do on Friday as the statement came out after New York trading hours.
They said the alliance deal looked like it was going to have to be renegotiated.

"It won't look too clever if they pay $20 billion for a company that won't be making much more than a billion dollars in 1998/99 with the possibility of further losses if they try to break into the local loop," Stiles said.
